claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr exhibits intrinsic local chemical heterogeneity with measurable chemical short-range order.
Diffraction or other local-structure techniques can validate the short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Experimentally calibrated Monte Carlo simulations can generate realistic short-range-order configurations for HfNbTaTiZr.
Using those configurations in separate Boltzmann transport models will produce independent lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity predictions.
The proposed approach will outperform models based on uniform Debye temperatures.
The method is intended to apply from 100 K to 1000 K.
Computational microstates can be constructed to mimic experimentally measured short-range-order levels in specimens with controlled processing histories.
Short-range-order motifs modulate local force constants.
Short-range-order motifs modulate the electronic band structure.
Variations in local chemical environments produce spatial variations in force-constant distributions and electron-scattering centers.
Modeling local-environment variations enables lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions to be predicted separately.
The predicted lattice thermal conductivity will differ by approximately 20–40% from averaged-model estimates.
The electronic thermal-conductivity channel will exhibit distinct low- and high-temperature trends.
The combined lattice and electronic predictions will yield total thermal conductivities of 10–17 W/(K m).
Prior analytical and simulation approaches generally assume perfect, defect-free crystals and use uniform Debye-temperature approximations for total thermal conductivity.
The model is applicable when short-range order can be reliably characterized in specimens with controlled processing and minimal extrinsic defects.
The model may not apply to heavily defected or highly oxidized specimens.
Changing measured short-range order through processing should produce corresponding changes in the independently measured lattice and electronic transport channels.
